modes.title: NCERT Line Hunter
modes.subject: Biology
modes.description: Tap the single altered word, then repair the NCERT statement.

challenges.sentence: The middle lamella is mainly composed of calcium carbonate.
challenges.explanation: The middle lamella is mainly composed of calcium pectate and holds neighbouring cells together.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Cell Wall · printed p.95

challenges.explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S particles, formed by 50S and 30S subunits.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Ribosomes and Inclusion Bodies · printed p.92

challenges.sentence: The cis face of the Golgi apparatus is the maturing face.
challenges.explanation: The trans face is the maturing face; the cis face is the forming face.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Golgi Apparatus · printed p.97

challenges.sentence: The nucleolus is a membrane-bound structure.
challenges.explanation: The nucleolus is not membrane-bound and is a site of active rRNA synthesis.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Nucleus · printed p.102

challenges.sentence: Chromoplasts contain chlorophyll and perform photosynthesis.
challenges.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and perform photosynthesis; chromoplasts contain other carotenoid pigments.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Plastids · printed p.99

modes.title: Diagram Detective
modes.subject: Biology
modes.description: Inspect NCERT-style diagrams and identify or repair their labels.

challenges.prompt: A label incorrectly calls the inner membrane folds ‘cisternae’. Which label repairs the diagram?
challenges.explanation: The inner mitochondrial membrane forms infoldings called cristae.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Mitochondria · printed p.99

challenges.prompt: Where do the hydrophobic lipid tails point in this bilayer?
options: Toward one another inside the bilayer
challenges.explanation: Hydrophobic tails face inward, while polar heads face the aqueous environments.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Cell Membrane · printed p.94

challenges.prompt: Which boundary outside the plasma membrane provides shape and mechanical support?
challenges.explanation: The cell wall lies outside the plasma membrane and provides shape and protection.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Cell Wall

challenges.prompt: Chromosomes aligned at the equatorial plate indicate which mitotic stage?
challenges.explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes align at the equatorial plate.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell Cycle and Cell Division · M Phase

challenges.prompt: What arrangement is shown in a typical eukaryotic cilium or flagellum?
challenges.explanation: Nine peripheral doublets surround two central microtubules: the 9 + 2 arrangement.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Cilia and Flagella · printed p.103

modes.title: Who Am I?
modes.subject: Mixed
modes.description: Reveal clues one at a time and identify the hidden NCERT term.

clues: I first saw and described a living cell.
challenges.explanation: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first observed and described a live cell.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Cell Theory · printed p.87

clues: I am secreted by the corpus luteum.
challenges.explanation: Progesterone supports the endometrium and helps maintain pregnancy.
challenges.source: Biology XII · Human Reproduction · Menstrual Cycle

clues: Kranz anatomy occurs in my leaves.
I am an important cereal crop.
challenges.explanation: Maize is a classic C4 plant with Kranz anatomy.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Photosynthesis in Higher Plants · C4 Pathway

clues: I attack the benzene ring during nitration.
challenges.explanation: The nitronium ion, NO₂⁺, is the electrophile in benzene nitration.
challenges.source: Chemistry XI · Hydrocarbons · Aromatic Hydrocarbons

clues: I proposed that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
My statement is associated with Omnis cellula-e cellula.
challenges.explanation: Rudolf Virchow explained that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Cell Theory · printed p.88

modes.title: Sequence Sprint
modes.subject: Biology
modes.description: Tap steps in the correct biological order before time runs out.

challenges.prompt: Arrange the stages of mitosis.
challenges.explanation: Mitosis progresses through prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell Cycle and Cell Division · M Phase

challenges.prompt: Arrange the path of air to the gas-exchange surface.
challenges.explanation: Air travels through this conducting pathway before reaching the alveoli.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Breathing and Exchange of Gases · Respiratory System

challenges.prompt: Arrange the flow of blood from the right ventricle to the left atrium.
challenges.explanation: Pulmonary circulation carries deoxygenated blood to lungs and oxygenated blood back to the left atrium.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Body Fluids and Circulation · Double Circulation

challenges.prompt: Arrange the major stages of glycolysis shown here.
challenges.explanation: Glucose is phosphorylated and rearranged before cleavage ultimately produces pyruvate.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Respiration in Plants · Glycolysis

challenges.prompt: Arrange the menstrual-cycle phases.
challenges.explanation: The menstrual phase is followed by follicular growth, ovulation and the luteal phase.
challenges.source: Biology XII · Human Reproduction · Menstrual Cycle

modes.title: NCERT Escape Room
modes.subject: Biology
modes.description: Solve five connected Cell City clues to unlock the laboratory exit.

challenges.prompt: Door 1: Select the organelle that modifies and packages material received from the ER.
challenges.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, packages and dispatches cellular material.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Golgi Apparatus

challenges.prompt: Door 2: Which Golgi face receives material from the ER?
challenges.explanation: The cis or forming face receives material from the ER.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Golgi Apparatus

challenges.prompt: Door 3: Which vesicle contains hydrolytic enzymes active at acidic pH?
challenges.explanation: Lysosomes contain acid hydrolases.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Lysosomes

challenges.prompt: Door 4: Which organelle produces most cellular ATP aerobically?
challenges.explanation: Mitochondria are major sites of aerobic respiration and ATP production.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Mitochondria

challenges.prompt: Door 5: Which nuclear structure actively synthesises rRNA?
challenges.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Nucleus

modes.title: Physics Rescue Lab
modes.subject: Physics
modes.description: Choose the right relation and calculate the value needed to repair the lab.

challenges.prompt: A 2 kg emergency cart accelerates at 3 m s⁻². What force restores its motion?
challenges.source: Physics XI · Laws of Motion · Newton's Second Law

challenges.prompt: A 10 N force moves a supply box 5 m in its direction. Calculate the work done.
challenges.explanation: Here θ = 0°, so W = 10 × 5 = 50 J.
challenges.source: Physics XI · Work, Energy and Power · Work

challenges.prompt: A 4 Ω safety resistor carries 2 A. What potential difference is required?
challenges.source: Physics XII · Current Electricity · Ohm's Law

challenges.prompt: A 2 μF capacitor is charged to 10 V. Find the stored energy.
challenges.source: Physics XII · Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance · Energy Stored

challenges.prompt: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 2 m. Find its speed.
challenges.source: Physics XI · Waves · Speed of a Travelling Wave

modes.title: Reaction Forge
modes.subject: Chemistry
modes.description: Combine substrate, reagent and condition to forge the correct product.

challenges.prompt: Forge the major product.
challenges.explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation adds H₂ across the double bond to form ethane.
challenges.source: Chemistry XI · Hydrocarbons · Alkenes

challenges.prompt: Forge the major organic product.
challenges.explanation: Nitration of benzene produces nitrobenzene through electrophilic substitution.
challenges.source: Chemistry XI · Hydrocarbons · Aromatic Hydrocarbons

challenges.prompt: Choose the substitution product.
challenges.explanation: Aqueous KOH replaces bromide with hydroxyl to form ethanol.
challenges.source: Chemistry XII · Haloalkanes and Haloarenes · Nucleophilic Substitution

challenges.prompt: What forms first?
challenges.explanation: Controlled oxidation of a primary alcohol first gives an aldehyde.
challenges.source: Chemistry XII · Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers · Oxidation

challenges.prompt: Complete the reaction.
challenges.explanation: Sodium reacts with water to produce sodium hydroxide and hydrogen.
challenges.source: Chemistry XI · The s-Block Elements · Group 1

modes.title: Spot the Impostor
modes.subject: Mixed
modes.description: Find the one statement that is not supported by NCERT.

challenges.prompt: Three statements describe mitochondria. Tap the impostor.
options: They are part of the endomembrane system.
challenges.explanation: Mitochondria are not considered part of the endomembrane system.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Endomembrane System

challenges.prompt: Three statements describe prokaryotes. Tap the impostor.
options: Their DNA lies in a nucleoid.
challenges.explanation: Prokaryotes do not possess membrane-bound mitochondria.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Prokaryotic Cells

challenges.prompt: Three statements describe enzymes. Tap the impostor.
options: Enzymes are consumed permanently in every reaction.
Their activity can depend on pH and temperature.
challenges.explanation: Enzymes act as catalysts and are not permanently consumed by the reaction.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Biomolecules · Enzymes

challenges.prompt: Three statements agree with Ohm's law conditions. Tap the impostor.
options: V is proportional to I at constant physical conditions.
The V-I graph is linear for an ohmic conductor.
Resistance must become zero when current increases.
challenges.explanation: For an ohmic conductor at constant conditions, resistance remains constant rather than becoming zero.
challenges.source: Physics XII · Current Electricity · Ohm's Law

challenges.prompt: Three statements describe benzene. Tap the impostor.
options: All carbon-carbon bonds have equal length.
It readily undergoes addition like an ordinary alkene.
challenges.explanation: Benzene characteristically undergoes electrophilic substitution and resists ordinary addition because of aromatic stability.
challenges.source: Chemistry XI · Hydrocarbons · Aromatic Hydrocarbons

modes.title: NCERT Treasure Hunt
modes.subject: Biology
modes.description: Use a hint to locate the correct NCERT section, diagram or page.

challenges.prompt: Find the NCERT location that explains Omnis cellula-e cellula.
challenges.hint: Look immediately after Schleiden and Schwann's original cell theory.
challenges.explanation: Virchow's modification of cell theory appears in the Cell Theory section.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · printed p.88

challenges.prompt: Where would you find the fluid mosaic model?
challenges.hint: Search the section describing lipids and proteins in the cell boundary.
challenges.explanation: Singer and Nicolson's fluid mosaic model is discussed under Cell Membrane.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · printed p.94

challenges.prompt: Locate the section containing cisternae with distinct cis and trans faces.
challenges.hint: This organelle packages and dispatches material.
challenges.explanation: Cis and trans faces are structural features of the Golgi apparatus.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Golgi Apparatus · printed p.97

challenges.prompt: Where is the 9 + 2 axoneme arrangement described?
challenges.hint: Search structures responsible for cellular movement.
challenges.explanation: The axoneme of cilia and flagella has the 9 + 2 arrangement.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Cilia and Flagella · printed p.103

challenges.prompt: Find the page discussing cristae and the mitochondrial matrix.
challenges.explanation: NCERT discusses mitochondrial membranes, cristae and matrix on printed page 99 in the indexed edition.
challenges.source: Biology XI · Cell: The Unit of Life · Mitochondria · printed p.99
